topic: Self-cancelling turn signal: a detent holds the stalk; a hinged finger meets the cancel cam on the steering shaft; it folds when the wheel turns into the turn and is rigid when the wheel turns back, so the cam knocks the stalk out of its detent.
title: How Does Your Blinker Turn Itself Off? 🚗
principle: The turn-signal stalk is held in a detent; a spring-biased pawl on the switch actuator projects next to a cancel cam fixed to the steering shaft. Turning into the signalled direction, the cam lobes tip the pawl aside without moving the stalk; turning back, a lobe drives the pawl against its stop, pushing the actuator out of its detent so the centering spring returns the stalk to neutral.
caption:
How Does Your Blinker Turn Itself Off? 🚗
Guess: what knocks the lever back? 👇
Follow @whyloop.hq for a new machine every day
#cars #howitworks #mechanism #engineering #driving
firstComment:
Answer: the steering wheel itself 🚗

When you flick the turn signal lever, a spring-loaded detent (a little notch) holds it in place, and a small hinged finger (often called a pawl) moves next to a cancel cam: a ring with bumps that is fixed to the steering shaft and turns with the wheel.

Turning into the corner, the bumps sweep past the finger and it simply folds out of the way, so the lever stays on.

Turning the wheel back, a bump hits the finger from the other side. Now it can't fold, so the push knocks the lever out of its notch and a spring returns it to the middle. The blinker stops.

That's also why a very gentle turn sometimes leaves the blinker on: the wheel never turns far enough for a bump to reach the finger.

(Simplified 3D model; real switches differ in detail.)

Sources:
US Patent 5,385,067, Turn signal cancellation mechanism (handle held in a detent position until the turn is completed; cancel cam with raised formations fixed to the steering shaft; the pawl is tipped aside on the way into the turn and pushed by the cam on the way back, returning the handle to neutral; a cancel return spring centers the handle): https://patents.google.com/patent/US5385067
YourMechanic, How does the turn signal switch know to reset (a cancel cam on the steering column presses the signal lever off as the wheel returns to center; gentle turns may need a manual cancel): https://www.yourmechanic.com/article/how-does-the-turn-signal-switch-know-to-reset-when-my-car-stops-turning

voiceover: How does your blinker know to turn itself off?
Flick the lever up, and a notch holds it there.
Inside, a hinged finger drops next to a bumpy ring on the steering shaft.
Turn right, and the bump just folds the finger out of the way.
Turn back, and the bump hits it from the other side, where it can't fold.
So it shoves the lever out of its notch, and the blinker stops.
Turning the wheel back knocks the lever home.
